IPT.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/7] The primary aim of this effectiveness trial was to extend findings from a prior efficacy trial to evaluate whether brief CB interventions reduced the incidence of MDD onset relative to brochure control when high school personnel recruited participants and delivered interventions.

male_pct.warning: Percentage of male participants is not reported in this section.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/10/Text/8] The simplified recruitment procedure applied in this effectiveness trial allowed students to selfselect into the program rather than research staff verifying that participants met a minimum level of depressive symptoms. [/page/12/Text/4] students with subthreshold depressive symptoms.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/11/Text/6] First, all of the outcomes relied on youth selfreport.

MedCat.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/9] With regard to the second aim, the CB group resulted in lower depressive symptoms than brochure control at posttest but not at 6-month follow-up. [/page/10/Text/5] With regard to the third aim, the CB group intervention had no detectable effects relative to either brochure control or CB bibliotherapy on either social adjustment (mean d = .20 and . 16 compared to brochure control and CB bibliotherapy, respectively) or substance use (mean d = .09 and .10 compared to brochure control and CB bibliotherapy, respectively).
